research_scope: Five full source-free mathematical reviews on locally free modules, module support, ideal radical and measure-theoretic raw moments; no source updates.

amendments.review_rationale: Read finite local freeness of an R-module on standard open covers of Spec(R), preserving localization, finite rank on each open and potentially varying rank across opens.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical source, current effective adjacency and domain/rank/measure scope. Preserved original wording while noting global mathematical audit concerns.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: a family of distinguished Zariski-open subsets D(f_i)={p∈Spec(R):f_i∉p} covering Spec(R), with at least one f_i outside every prime p.
references.reason: Standard-open covers are reusable local data for schemes/modules, distinct from the locally-free property imposed on localizations.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.phrase: free module of finite rank over R_{f_i}
references.context: Module theory: free module of finite rank n over the localized commutative ring R_{f_i}, isomorphic to R_{f_i}^{⊕n} for some finite n≥0, allowing n to depend on i.
references.reason: Finite-rank freeness is a reusable module property distinct from the weaker unrestricted free module and from the cover condition.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.phrase: rank allowed to vary by open set
references.disposition: Finite local freeness need not mean global constant rank or globally free module.

amendments.review_rationale: Read local freeness of an R-module on basic Zariski open cover, with module and ring localization and free modules of possibly infinite and variable rank.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical source, current effective adjacency and domain/rank/measure scope. Preserved original wording while noting global mathematical audit concerns.

references.phrase: cover of Spec(R) by standard opens D(f_i)
references.context: Algebraic geometry: family of distinguished opens D(f_i) in Spec(R) with union equal to Spec(R); the f_i need not all be the same and the localizations are taken on these opens.
references.reason: Zariski standard-open covers are independently reusable and should be compared with the related finite-locally-free occurrence during the post-pass audit.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.context: Module theory: module over the localized ring R_{f_i} admitting a (possibly infinite) basis and therefore isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of R_{f_i}; no finite-rank assumption here.
references.reason: Freeness over a localized ring is independently reusable and must not be conflated with finite-rank freeness.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.phrase: locally free need not be finite locally free
references.disposition: No finite-rank condition appears in the local freeness statement.

amendments.review_rationale: Read support of finite module as primes whose localized module is nonzero and the closedness conclusion under Noetherianity, preserving the prime-spectrum and localization requirements.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical source, current effective adjacency and domain/rank/measure scope. Preserved original wording while noting global mathematical audit concerns.

references.disposition: The predicate M_p≠0 is the defining membership test for p in Supp_R(M); module localization is already linked and nonzero is foundational.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: Zariski-closed subset of Spec(R), equivalently V(I)={p∈Spec(R):I⊆p} for some ideal I of R; here the support of a finite module is V(Ann_R M).
references.reason: The Zariski closed-set notion is independently reusable. Mathematical-scope audit: for finitely generated modules this support is closed even without requiring R Noetherian.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.phrase: support of finite module is Zariski closed
references.disposition: Closedness is a consequence of finiteness (indeed holds for finite modules more generally), separate from the definition using nonzero localizations.

references.phrase: local ring with maximal ideal m

references.context: Commutative algebra: radical sqrt(I)={r∈R:r^n∈I for some positive integer n} of an ideal I in a commutative ring R.
references.reason: The radical is a reusable ideal operation, distinct from the specific local-ring condition sqrt(I)=m.

references.context: Commutative algebra: m-primary ideal I of a Noetherian local ring (R,m), with sqrt(I)=m and I primary; in this Noetherian local setting radical m is equivalent to m-primary.
references.reason: Primary ideals are reusable and should not be conflated with prime ideals or maximal ideals; record Noetherian-local equivalence explicitly.

amendments.review_rationale: Read nth raw moment of nonnegative Borel or Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure as integral of x^n over real interval, conditioned on integrability; distinguish from centered moments.
amendments.reason: Reviewed whole mathematical source, current effective adjacency and domain/rank/measure scope. Preserved original wording while noting global mathematical audit concerns.

references.context: Measure theory: Lebesgue integral ∫_{(a,b)} x^n dμ(x) of a measurable real power function with respect to a Borel/Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure μ on a real interval, with endpoint conventions according to source.
references.reason: The integral relative to a measure is independently reusable; it is not the raw moment itself without the chosen exponent and measure.
references.matching_note: Provisional source-free contextual prerequisite, pending deduplication and source verification.

references.context: Measure theory: μ-integrability of x↦x^n means measurability and ∫_{(a,b)}|x|^n dμ(x)<∞, for n a nonnegative integer, under the conventional finite-L1 meaning of integrable.
references.reason: Integrability is independently reusable; flag that the source's additional 'finite only when integral finite' may be redundant given its integrability assumption.
